source_choice: John prefers option 6 (tomato with blossom-end rot) from the preceding contact sheets; asked for a slightly riper tomato and colour/ripeness variations.
prompt:
Create ONE comparison contact sheet of EXACTLY SIX colour/ripeness variations of the SAME TOMATO PHOTOGRAPH.

SOURCE: the attached reference is a six-photo contact sheet. Use ONLY photograph 6, the BOTTOM-RIGHT tomato photograph, as the image to edit. Ignore the other five photographs entirely. The user chose number 6 as the strongest composition and wants the main tomato to look a little riper. We are comparing tomato COLOUR, not new compositions.

Keep the photographic scene almost identical in all six variants: the exact framing, camera angle, main round tomato's shape and size, its position in the upper-middle foreground, green calyx, hairy stems, the two unripe green tomatoes behind/right, surrounding leaves, softly blurred greenhouse frame, lighting, depth of field, surface texture and shadows. The dark brown-black sunken blossom-end-rot patch at the bottom/front of the main tomato MUST remain the SAME size, location and texture in every variant. Keep the withered flower remnant at its centre. Only recolour the healthy skin of the MAIN foreground tomato to compare natural ripening stages. Preserve natural pale specular highlights and tiny surface texture; no flat paint fill. Background fruit remain green in all six. No changes to exposure, white balance or overall image grading.

Layout: exactly 3 columns x 2 rows of equal portrait photographs, each approximately185:240 aspect ratio, with narrow warm ivory gutters and small warm ivory label strips beneath, matching the reference contact-sheet layout. Overall canvas nearly square landscape, approximately1320x1194 or higher. Large simple black letter labels A,B,C in the first row, D,E,F in the second row, OUTSIDE the photos. No numbers, no other text, no title, no book page overlay. Six complete portrait images.

Colour sequence, clearly distinguishable but all realistically photographic:
A — just a little riper than source: mostly warm apricot/orange, still a small yellow-green transition near lower sides, less green than original.
B — warm ripe tangerine-orange across nearly all healthy skin, slight golden variation, no obvious green area.
C — orange-red blush, richer coral/vermilion upper and front surfaces grading naturally to warm orange along lower side, convincingly turning red.
D — mostly bright tomato-red with a faint orange shoulder/highlight region, an inviting nearly ripe red tomato, natural unevenness.
E — fully ripe classic natural scarlet-red, subtle variation and realistic highlights, no orange-dominant or green skin.
F — slightly deeper fully ripe red than E, rich restrained red with fine natural tonal variation; do NOT make it purple, burgundy, black, desaturated, excessively shiny, wrinkled or overripe. Healthy skin stays firm.

Retain the original natural editorial greenhouse photography quality. The rot should remain conspicuous and biologically plausible against every skin colour, without becoming larger, wetter or more gruesome. All six frames must read as the SAME photograph with only the main tomato's ripeness colour changed. This is an artistic colour-selection sheet, not a scientific time-lapse or an instructional ripening sequence.
review: Visually inspected all six labelled panels A–F. Main tomato colour progresses from orange to red; composition, green background fruit and blossom-end-rot patch are substantially consistent. No layout or print-readiness approval implied.
production_gate: Trial artwork first; paid subscription/upscale deferred. Before printer upload if adopted, upscale chosen low-resolution artwork, inspect and verify at least 300 ppi at final placement. Production PDFs and approved masters unchanged.
selection_note: John selected C and requested the section page with contents and folio; layout proposal is in ../2026-11-24-troubles-tomato-opener-04/.
